root_idea.summary: The root centers on drawing or extending something out gently and covertly.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop extraction and selection, discreet removal or theft, offspring as something drawn out, connected or chain-like forms, flowing water, channels, and figurative wasting or loss.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form V verb normalized to its Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
Quran-attested nominal form with an established dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To slip away, withdraw, or go out secretly and unobtrusively.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for a person or group leaving from among others covertly or gradually; the Quran occurrence is the imperfect plural form يَتَسَلَّلُونَ.

senses.definition: An extract or essence drawn from something; hence a pure, selected, or choice portion, especially an extract from earth or clay.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ, it denotes what is drawn or selected from the substance of the earth or clay.

senses.definition: A reproductive extract or seminal fluid, understood as what is drawn out for generation.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported Quranic interpretation of سُلَالَةٌ in the creation passage; it presents the reproductive fluid as an extract rather than defining every occurrence of the word in this way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw or pull something out or forth, especially gently; also to take or draw something away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes drawing a sword from its sheath or a hair from dough, and taking a dead body head-first toward a grave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal or draw something away covertly, secretly, or clandestinely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be removed from among comparable objects, as a camel from among other camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lose one's teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, sheep, goat, or an extremely old she-camel whose teeth have fallen out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become affected by the disease called سِلّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive-form usage referring to contraction of the wasting pulmonary disease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal, especially covertly, secretly, or clandestinely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV verb may take the thing stolen, as in stealing from spoil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An open raid or predatory incursion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun associated with the Form IV lexical family, distinct from its senses of theft and bribery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid another person in stealing or in stealing secretly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or assistance construction of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to be affected by the disease called سِلّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become agitated or in a state of commotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An additional Form V usage explained through the image of repeated drawing out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become drawn or pulled out gently; to slip out from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a sword slipping from its sheath or a leading-rope coming out of a person's hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slip away or steal away covertly, secretly, or gradually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe going forth from among people or leaving deliberately and by degrees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a river to give off a rivulet or streamlet branching from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form X construction used of a watercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Connection or being connected with another thing; hence binding or fastening with a chain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe the act of connecting or the resulting binding by a سِلْسِلَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The continuous pouring or passing of liquid into the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same image explains the expression for not eating food, as though it were not passed into the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat a long piece taken from a camel's hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verb usage attributed to a lexical authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water to run or descend in a continuous, chain-like or rippling course; for lightning to form elongated chain-like streams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water entering the throat or running down a declivity, and of lightning assuming chain-like forms in clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a sword's varied wavy marks, streaks, or grain to glisten and appear to creep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description based on chain-like or rippling appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a garment to become thin through prolonged wear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of progressive wearing or loosening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Consumption or phthisis, a wasting and often fatal disease associated with pulmonary ulceration or persistent cough and fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word has variant vocalizations and is also represented by related forms such as سُلَالٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figurative wasting away or loss of property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use likening the diminution of wealth to the wasting of the body through the disease سِلّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The drawing of swords or the occasion of drawing swords.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of action used in expressions for coming upon people when swords are drawn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Theft, especially covert, secret, or clandestine theft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A simple noun corresponding in meaning to the verbal noun إِسْلَالٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse's rush among other horses or its burst of speed in striving to outstrip them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative equestrian use describing a forceful competitive advance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse's revulsion or release of shortness of breath in the chest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the respiratory episode produced when the horse suppresses such breathlessness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Power or force of long continuance in a sheep or goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal husbandry usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A basket or receptacle, especially one used for carrying fruit or bread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote a woven or covered basket and has several recorded plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fault, breach, or fissure through which water escapes or is absorbed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a defect in a watering-trough, tank, or jar, and of fissures in the ground that take up water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sewing a skin or hide with two thongs through a single puncture or stitch-hole.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drawn sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal result associated with being drawn out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A child or offspring, as something brought forth or drawn out from its parent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related feminine form is used for a daughter; the sense is not restricted to one sex in general reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A colt; with the feminine ending, a filly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal term with additional recorded distinctions concerning the circumstances of birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A newly born camel before its sex is known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for a young camel immediately after birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clear, pure, cool, or easily swallowed beverage or wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description emphasizes removal of turbidity and ease of descent into the throat; it can refer to a beverage of Paradise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A water channel or watercourse in a valley; also a valley or low place where water flows or collects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers the main channel of a valley, a broad or deep valley, and a narrow torrent channel; a related figurative phrase describes swift travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The brain of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hump of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical or culinary usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The spinal cord.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strip or portion of flesh, especially portions designated as خَصِيل.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective expression سَلِيلُ اللَّحْمِ has the plural سَلَائِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sinew or elongated portion of flesh, including strips running along the backbone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote an oblong flesh portion, a thin flesh-like substance, or long slices from a camel's hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblong portion or lump of dried mucus or similar matter in the nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is used for such nasal portions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion of separated goat hair drawn out for spinning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hair is divided, folded, tied, and drawn out portion by portion as it is spun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain long fish with a long beak-like snout.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of baskets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tentatively reported occupational usage for the maker of baskets called سِلَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sweet, clear, cool water that enters the throat easily; also mellow wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The water may be limpid through settling and movement; the wine sense emphasizes sweetness, clarity, and easy swallowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pool left by a torrent whose surface becomes rippled like a chain when stirred by wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the appearance of standing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light, active, or energetic boy or young man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized personal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A long piece of a camel's hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun distinct from the connection and chain senses of the same written form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chain of connected metal rings or similar links.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The chain could be stretched across a river or road to stop boats, beasts, or travelers for collection of dues.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An elongated or chain-like formation, especially a stream of lightning or an extended accumulation of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural usage describes chain-shaped lightning in clouds or sands accumulated and extended one upon another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A line or series of lines in a book or piece of writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually occurring in the plural for lines of text.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Chain-like marks visible on a horse's legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative appearance-based description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small spotted reptile or lizard with a slender moving tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who draws or pulls something out or forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle of سَلَّ; the same form can also be used for a thief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thief, especially one who steals covertly or secretly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized active-participial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bribe, or the giving or receiving of a bribe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun used in the reported expression contrasting bribery or theft with treachery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Theft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same established noun in the reported expression; distinct from the open-raid sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something slender and drawn out, especially a green palm-stick or sword used as an image for a slender sleeping-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in a fixed descriptive expression and is explained as an infinitive used in the sense of a passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large or packing needle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is مَسَالُّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Subtle or crafty in the machinations of theft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial description of a stealthy thief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose testicles have been extracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An elliptical anatomical use of the passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by the disease called سِلّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participle associated with the disease sense of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheep or goat whose powers or strength are of long continuance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal description recorded under the related passive-participial form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having its parts or portions connected one with another; hence chained or bound with a chain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The connected-parts and physically chained senses belong to the same participial branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lightning forming chain-like shapes in its upper portions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative appearance-based usage, sometimes associated with rain that follows reliably.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hair that is rippled, crisp, curly, twisted, or contracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description compares the hair's succession of waves with chain-like running water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword bearing varied wavy marks, streaks, or grain like a chain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative participial description of the sword's surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment marked with stripes or lines, or woven badly and thinly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle describes either a striped pattern or thin, poor weaving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A report transmitted through an uninterrupted chain of narrators linked by a repeated meeting or formula.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical hadith term derived from the idea of continuous connection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment worn until it has become thin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized participial usage describing progressive wear.

cautions: The Classical evidence is indexed under Lane's contracted geminate root سل; many listed derivatives are broader Classical Arabic evidence and are not Quran-attested forms.
The Quranic سُلَالَةٌ passage is explicitly explained both as an extract or selected essence and, in one interpretation, as a reproductive extract; these are kept as distinct but related senses.
The Lane Quran reference attached to سُلَالَةٌ is reported as a classical citation and is not used as an independently generated modern verse location beyond the QAC-supplied occurrences.
